title: Dedicated: backfill scaling policy defaults + migrations (preserve legacy behavior until opt-in)
author: Michael Nguyen
description:
Context: We added new per-deployment scaling policy fields (min/max bounds, cooldowns, predictive mode). For existing Dedicated deployments we must not change autoscaling behavior until the feature flag is enabled per account/deployment. This PR adds DB migrations + a backfill job that (a) preserves legacy scaling semantics by default, (b) makes the new policy evaluation deterministic by ensuring all existing rows have explicit defaults where needed, and (c) adds safety checks/metrics to avoid accidental rollout impact.

What this PR does:
- Adds schema migration for scaling_policy columns on Dedicated deployments:
  - scaling_policy_mode: ENUM('legacy','policy_v1') (default: 'legacy')
  - scaling_policy_v1: JSONB (nullable)
  - scaling_policy_updated_at, scaling_policy_updated_by (nullable; populated only when policy_v1 is used)
  - scaling_policy_backfill_version: INT (for idempotency + audit)
- Introduces a backfill job (idempotent, resumable) that sets explicit legacy defaults for all existing Dedicated deployments:
  - scaling_policy_mode='legacy'
  - scaling_policy_v1 remains NULL (so control plane evaluation path continues to use legacy autoscaler config)
  - scaling_policy_backfill_version set to current migration version
- Adds safety checks to prevent unintended behavior changes:
  - Hard guard: if feature flag dedicated_scaling_policy_v1 is disabled, policy evaluation returns legacy config regardless of any JSONB contents
  - Validator rejects mixed states (e.g., policy_v1 JSON present while mode='legacy') unless initiated by the control plane "enable" endpoint
  - Migration includes a post-migration verification query that fails the deploy if any row violates invariants
- Adds rollout knobs:
  - Backfill runs in batches (default 2k rows) with adaptive sleep and can be stopped/restarted safely
  - Supports dry-run mode (logs counts + sample IDs only)
  - Emits metrics: dedicated_scaling_policy_backfill_rows_total, dedicated_scaling_policy_backfill_errors_total, dedicated_scaling_policy_invariant_violations_total

Why we need explicit backfill (vs relying on implicit DB defaults):
- We need deterministic behavior across regions and read replicas: older rows may have NULLs depending on write path.
- Control plane caching + policy evaluation requires stable "effective config" computation for auditability.
- We want to distinguish "legacy" deployments from "policy_v1" deployments without relying on presence/absence of JSON.

Safety invariants (enforced by migration + runtime):
- Existing Dedicated deployments remain on legacy path until opt-in.
- No deployment can enter policy_v1 without both (1) feature flag enabled for the account and (2) explicit mode switch.
- Backfill must be safe to rerun and safe during partial deploys (one region ahead).

Implementation notes:
- Backfill uses a WHERE clause on scaling_policy_backfill_version IS DISTINCT FROM <version> to avoid rewrites.
- Uses UPDATE ... WHERE id IN (SELECT id ... LIMIT N FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) to minimize lock contention.
- Adds a small helper in capacity-policy-service to compute effective mode with precedence: featureFlag -> mode -> legacy fallback.

Illustrative snippet (simplified):
- "WITH cte AS (SELECT id FROM dedicated_deployments WHERE scaling_policy_backfill_version IS DISTINCT FROM 3 ORDER BY id LIMIT $1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) UPDATE dedicated_deployments d SET scaling_policy_mode='legacy', scaling_policy_backfill_version=3, updated_at=NOW() FROM cte WHERE d.id=cte.id"

Test plan:
- Unit tests:
  - idempotent backfill does not change already-backfilled rows
  - invariant checks catch invalid mixed states
  - feature flag gate forces legacy behavior even if JSON is present
- Integration tests (sqlite + postgres in CI):
  - migration applies cleanly from prior schema
  - backfill runs in batches and completes
- Manual:
  - ran dry-run in staging; verified counts match expected Dedicated deployments; verified no changes in autoscaler desired replicas logs

Rollout plan:
- Land migrations + backfill tooling behind deploy-time toggle (runs after migration only in prod once).
- Canary in us-east-1 control plane first.
- Only after verification, enable account-level feature flag for pilot accounts via INT-9412 process.

Follow-ups:
- Once GA, consider setting scaling_policy_mode default to 'policy_v1' for new deployments created under eligible plans, but keep explicit creation-time semantics in the API.

Risk:
- Migration touches dedicated_deployments; risk of long-running updates. Mitigated via SKIP LOCKED batching + adaptive sleep + metrics/abort.

References:
- Linear: ENG-22153 (Migration defaults), ENG-22141 (Schema/API), PM-1842 (Epic)
- Related PRs: pr-48211 (schema fields), pr-48252 (Console endpoints)

Checklist:
- [x] Backward-compatible by default
- [x] Idempotent migrations/backfill
- [x] Metrics emitted for backfill progress/errors
- [x] Staging validation completed
- [x] SRE review requested for rollout safety

review_conversation: Ethan Park: Can we guarantee no behavior change if someone accidentally writes scaling_policy_v1 JSON directly to the DB? I want a hard runtime guard, not just migration defaults.

Michael Nguyen (author): Yep—added a feature-flag gate in effective mode computation. If dedicated_scaling_policy_v1 is off, we ignore policy_v1 entirely and always return legacy config. Also added invariant check to reject mixed states via API.
Vanessa Ortiz: Backfill UPDATE pattern—please avoid table-wide write amplification. Can we use SKIP LOCKED batches and emit progress metrics? Also ensure it won’t fight with autoscaler reads.

Michael Nguyen (author): Updated to SKIP LOCKED batching (2k default) with adaptive sleep. Autoscaler reads are unaffected since it’s control-plane only; we also only touch a few columns. Added metrics + dry-run.
Rafael Mendes: Post-migration verification query—what happens on violation? We should fail the deploy and page, not silently continue.
Michael Nguyen (author): Agreed. Verification runs as a deploy step; non-zero violations fail the release pipeline in that region. Metrics also emitted for alerting during canary.
Jordan Lee: The enum default 'legacy' is good, but make sure new deployment creation explicitly sets mode based on plan/flag. Don’t rely on DB defaults long term.

Michael Nguyen (author): Added TODO in service layer and left DB default as legacy specifically to preserve existing behavior. New deployment path will be handled in ENG-22141 follow-up wiring once feature flag is on.
Ethan Park: Please add one more test that simulates partial rollout (one region on new code, one on old) and ensures old readers don’t break when seeing the new columns.
Michael Nguyen (author): Added integration test that applies migration and runs legacy read path; verifies no deserialization issues for old payload shapes.
Rafael Mendes: Approved once CI passes and the runbook link is in the PR description.
Michael Nguyen (author): Added runbook link + rollout notes.
